frontmatter.title: How to Load Notebooks Python

blocks.content: Developers seeking to load OneNote files (e.g., .one) into Python applications using Aspose.Note must use the `aspose_note_foss` package. The library provides core classes to open and parse notebook structures, enabling programmatic access to pages, sections, and content.
Aspose.Note -- Required installation and import statements.
For details on prerequisites, see the Aspose.Note documentation.

Aspose.Note enables loading Microsoft OneNote files directly in Python using the `Document` class. Developers can load notebooks from local file paths, byte streams, or `Stream` objects, depending on their application’s architecture and requirements.

Loading from a file path is the most common scenario and supports both `.one` and `.onepkg` formats. For programmatic flexibility, loading from a stream allows integration with in-memory data sources such as uploaded files or network responses. The `LoadOptions` class provides optional configuration for handling encrypted notebooks or specifying password credentials during load.

When using `LoadOptions`, ensure the `password` property is set only for password-protected notebooks to avoid unnecessary errors. The library handles format detection automatically, so explicit format specification is not required for standard OneNote files.

This section demonstrates how to load a notebook file using Aspose.Note in Python. The example shows opening a .one file, inspecting its structure, and printing a summary of its contents. Aspose.Note provides the Notebook class to represent a notebook document, and the Document class for individual pages. The library supports loading from file paths and exposes basic metadata for inspection.

import aspose_note_foss

# Load a notebook from file
notebook = aspose_note_foss.Notebook("sample.one")

# Print summary: number of child documents
print(f"Notebook contains {len(notebook.child_nodes)} child documents.")
Aspose.Note supports loading multiple notebook and note file formats in Python. The `aspose_note_foss` package enables programmatic access to these formats via the `Notebook` class.

| Format | Extension | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| OneNote 2007–2016 | .one | Standard OneNote file format |
| OneNote Notebook | .onepkg | OneNote package format |
| PDF | .pdf | Portable Document Format |
| HTML | .html | HyperText Markup Language |
| Markdown | .md | Lightweight markup language |
| Text | .txt | Plain text file |
| JPEG | .jpg | JPEG image format |
| PNG | .png | Portable Network Graphics |
| BMP | .bmp | Bitmap image format |
| TIFF | .tiff | Tagged Image File Format |
